items.title: LEGO fans have 2 more GTA store openings to track after Markham store launch, with Toronto and Mississauga dates confirmed
items.summary: The LEGO Group officially opened its first Markham LEGO Store at CF Markville on Sept. 11. New GTA LEGO store locations are set to open in Mississauga and Toronto by December, on the heels of a new LEGO store opening in Markham on Sept. 11. Spanning approximately 2,690 square feet, the Markham location offers are plenty of places to see new products and speak with staff about creating your own LEGO masterpiece. The next LEGO store destination to open will be at the CF Toronto Eaton Centre, with 2,637 square feet of space for LEGO building, playing and buying. The final location set to open in Ontario this year is at the Square One Shopping Centre in Mississauga, with 2,970 square feet — the largest of the three. Hiring is already underway for the other new locations. com, fans won’t have to wait too long to explore the newest LEGO stores. The Toronto location is set to open Oct. 23, while the Mississauga store is scheduled to welcome shoppers Nov. 6.

items.title: Financial help on the way for Mississauga businesses hurt by U.S. tariffs
items.summary: S. tariffs amid the ongoing trade war between Canada and its closest neighbour will receive property tax relief and other aid as the city seeks to ease their financial burden. S. President Donald Trump on Aug. 22. S. on Aug. 21 and subsequent tariffs “present a significant and ongoing threat to Mississauga’s businesses and workers,” City of Mississauga officials said earlier. The motion adopted on Wednesday, which was tabled by Mayor Carolyn Parrish, includes several ways in which the city can help businesses weather the storm brought on by the tension in trade relations between the two countries. Property tax relief in 2027 for businesses Among the options to be investigated by staff are a “broad property class or general tax payment relief for the 2027 tax year,” property tax deferrals for businesses feeling financial hardship due to the tariffs, an application-based tax instalment deferral program, grant funding opportunities and other initiatives. Senior city staff will now evaluate the various options and report back to council as soon as possible. In supporting the motion on Wednesday, several councillors spoke about the importance of protecting Mississauga businesses and suggested the city keep provincial and federal governments in the loop as they could offer help as well.

items.title: Mississauga taking action on tariffs: City exploring additional business supports as trade uncertainty continues
items.summary: A range of business competitiveness and resilience measures, including tax relief, economic development and procurement initiatives and development-related tools will be explored. Economic Development | September 16, 2026 As Canada responds to the latest trade measures from the United States that include new tariffs and import restrictions affecting key sectors of the economy, City Council approved a motion today to direct staff to explore a range of support measures for businesses affected by tariffs. The motion directs City staff to review and report to back to Council on: The motion follows an update to Council at the City’s General Committee meeting on September 9 about the impact of trade tariffs. The update focused on the key role Partners in Trade plays in the current trade climate. Watch the video from the September 9 General Committee meeting. See the PowerPoint presentation. In an effort to strengthen local economic resilience, protect jobs and alleviate financial pressure for local businesses and workers in Mississauga, the review will examine potential tax relief programs, investment and economic development initiatives, planning incentives, grant opportunities and procurement strategies, with recommendations to be presented to Council at a future meeting. As Ontario’s second largest economy and key contributor to the federal government’s Build Canada priority, Mississauga is taking action to help businesses respond to trade uncertainty, compete in new markets and strengthen long-term growth. Through Partners in Trade, the City is focused on connecting businesses to opportunities, advocating for local priorities and building a more resilient economy.

items.title: Mississauga pulls plug on big new data centres for 1 year
items.summary: Flashing beacons, digital speed display signs and pavement m… If approved, the exemption will only apply to one Ward 2 res… 20-plus residents showed up to oppose a proposed data centre — now Mississauga has a city-wide one-year freeze. Council unanimously approved the one-year pause on all new digital infrastructure with a total peak power demand of 10 megawatts or greater. Mississauga city council has passed a one-year moratorium on new major data centres while staff study environmental, land-use and infrastructural impacts. The temporary interim control bylaw was approved at the Sept. 16 council meeting and applies to all citywide facilities with a peak power demand of 10 megawatts or greater. While existing and already approved digital facilities will continue to operate, they cannot expand their operations if it pushes their peak demand to 10 megawatts or more. Facilities requiring under 10 megawatts are exempt from this ban, according to the bylaw document.

items.title: Japanese restaurant opens location at Heartland Town Centre in Mississauga

It’s the second location in the city—the first is on Confederation Parkway, near Square One Shopping Centre. items.title: Massive street food festival returns to Mississauga’s Cooksville
items.summary: One of Mississauga’s biggest food festivals is even bigger this year, with nearly 100 vendors and extended hours. Taste of Cooksville, organized by the Cooksville Business Improvement Area is back on Sept. 19 and 20 for a weekend of delicious food, live music, family entertainment, and more in the historic Cooksville neighbourhood. Like previous years, the festival is free for everyone to attend. There’s even more time to enjoy the food and festivities with extended hours, running from 11 am to 11 pm on Saturday, Sept. 19 and 11 am to 8 pm on Sunday, Sept. 20. Nearly one hundred vendors and food trucks will be lined up along 47 Dundas St W near Hurontario, offering sweet and savoury cuisine from around the world. There’ll be a ton of variety, making it easy to turn a trip to the festival into a full afternoon or evening of eating and exploring. Pair your food with a refreshingly cold drink from the beer garden, presented by Port Credit’s Old Credit Brewing Co. While trying some delicious eats, enjoy nonstop live music and performances on the main stage, bouncy inflatables, workshops and activities for the kids, and a brand-new car show putting an exciting lineup of vehicles on display. More info on vendors and entertainment will be posted soon on the event’s website. Taste of Cooksville is one of the city’s most popular yearly events since 2019, and is now among the biggest food festivals in the GTA.

items.title: Mississauga jeweller accused in $24-million Pearson gold heist has charge dropped
items.summary: Virtually all of the loot remains unaccounted for after the brazen gold-and-cash theft at Toronto’s Pearson International Airport on April 17, 2023. Ali Raza, a Mississauga jeweller, had the charge against him related to the 2023 Pearson gold heist, dropped in a court hearing Wednesday. Mississauga jeweller Ali Raza blinked away tears but said he was happy outside the Brampton courthouse on Wednesday, minutes after hearing he is no longer facing a charge of receiving stolen goods from the largest gold heist in Canadian history. He had been charged with knowingly receiving large amounts of gold stolen at Pearson airport on April 17, 2023. “Ali’s life was destroyed,” his lawyer Brij Mohan said, standing close to his client. “His family life was destroyed. ” “I am innocent,” Raza, 37, said, his eyes watering. ” In a brief court hearing Wednesday, Crown attorney Jelena Vlacic said they made the decision to stop the proceedings against Raza based on new evidence. Vlacic said that evidence is covered under a publication ban and cannot be reported at this time.

items.title: Save energy and money with efficient home upgrades
items.summary: Make your home more energy efficient, attend a workshop or check out online resources to learn about programs that can help pay for energy upgrades. Fall is almost here. Now is a good time to prepare your home for cooler weather and explore ways to lower your energy bills. Small changes can help you stay comfortable and save energy without turning up the heat. They will also help to make Mississauga a more climate-friendly city. In 2024, residential buildings across Mississauga produced roughly 15 per cent of the city’s greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Homeowners can help reduce emissions by making their homes more energy efficient. If you need help getting started, sign up for a home energy coaching session. For example, the Centre for Community Energy Transformation (CCET), a non-profit organization serving Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon, provides a coaching session for free. An energy coach can help you understand your options and create a plan. Toronto and Region Conservation Authority (TRCA) also offers a free one-on-one consultation through its Climate Ready Homes Program, where residents will receive resources to help them save energy and water, reduce waste, create sustainable gardens and improve the comfort of their homes. In addition to these free coaching services, homeowners can also get a more detailed home energy assessment to see where their home is losing energy. This is a paid service offered by independent energy auditors. After the assessment is complete, the auditor will provide the homeowner with a personalized report that identifies upgrades that could help save money and energy.

items.title: A City in Tune returns to celebrate the music and musicians that helped shape Mississauga
items.summary: The Museums of Mississauga exhibit runs from September 24 to December 27, 2026. Entertainment and activities | September 14, 2026 Back for the second year, A City in Tune: Mississauga’s Greatest Hits, returns to Adamson Estate from September 24 to December 27, 2026. Presented by the Museums of Mississauga, the exhibit explores the people, places and sounds that have helped define Mississauga’s music story. This all-new exhibition invites visitors to listen, reflect and learn about Mississauga’s impressive and diverse musical talent. Explore artifacts, instruments and archival materials from artists such as Triumph, Donna Grantis and Billy Talent. See large-scale portraits of some of the city’s best-known musicians, check out a map of iconic music venues and attractions, and listen to curated playlists featuring artists connected to Mississauga. Join the Museums team on Saturday, September 26 for the opening reception. This is your opportunity to be among the first to explore the exhibit and celebrate the homegrown talent, memorable moments and local stories behind Mississauga’s music history. A City in Tune: Mississauga’s Greatest Hits exhibition Adamson Estate 850 Enola Ave. m.
